blocks.headline: 90 days of food and water, *without going broke*.
blocks.narration: Nobody can buy ninety days of supplies in one trip. So don't. Build it one payday at a time.
blocks.scene: a well organized pantry shelf with canned goods, rice, beans and jars, warm farmhouse light

blocks.headline: Stage 1: *72 hours*.
lines: g|Water, a flashlight, your medicines, a little cash
blocks.narration: Stage one is seventy two hours. Water, a flashlight, your medicines, and a little cash.
blocks.scene: a flashlight, water bottles, a pill organizer and folded cash on a wooden kitchen table

blocks.headline: Stage 2: *two weeks* at home.
blocks.narration: Stage two is two weeks at home, which is what the American Red Cross recommends.
blocks.scene: stacked water jugs and canned food in a tidy closet of a country home

blocks.headline: Stage 3: *30 days*.
blocks.narration: Stage three is thirty days. Only the food you already eat, rotated into normal meals so nothing goes to waste.
blocks.scene: a woman's hands placing jars of home canned vegetables on a pantry shelf, soft morning light

blocks.headline: Stage 4: *90 days*.
blocks.narration: Stage four is ninety days, built slowly, with nothing wasted. One payday at a time.
blocks.scene: a full farmhouse pantry at golden hour, shelves of food and water neatly labeled

blocks.headline: Comment *READY*
blocks.narration: Comment ready, and we'll message you the ninety day kit. Thirteen printable pages, nine dollars.
blocks.scene: a printed home emergency checklist on a clipboard on a kitchen table beside a mug of coffee and a pencil, morning window light
